title: A mixin that writes operators for you
description:
The Curiously Recurring Template Pattern: a class inherits from a template **instantiated with itself**. The base then knows the derived type at compile time and can call into it with no virtual functions.

Write `template <typename Derived> struct Comparable`. Any class that inherits from `Comparable<Itself>` and provides `==` and `<` gets the other four comparisons for free:

| Operator | Defined as |
|---|---|
| `a != b` | `!(a == b)` |
| `a > b` | `b < a` |
| `a <= b` | `!(b < a)` |
| `a >= b` | `!(a < b)` |

Write them as `friend` functions inside `Comparable`, taking `const Derived&` parameters.
hints: Inside `Comparable<Derived>`, each operator is a hidden friend: `friend bool operator!=(const Derived& a, const Derived& b) { return !(a == b); }`.
The derived class writes `struct Version : Comparable<Version>` and only defines `==` and `<`.
